description: Conjures Orbital Skyhooks (typeID 81080) onto every planet of a solar system that does not have one, and removes them again, without consuming an item, without a ship and without the caller being in the system. /ash anchor here|<systemID> deploys one Skyhook per free planet just past that planet's warp-in point - the single spot a warp to the planet always lands on, read from the game's own getClientParityWarpInPoint, offset further out (offsetMeters, default 25 km) so a ship warping in does not materialise inside the model, and changeable in game with /ash offset - falling back to a horizontal star-facing placement at the larger of a configurable standoff and one planet radius for bodies the game has no warp-in point for, and reports the split (deployed, already present, over a destroyed skyhook); /ash remove <skyhookID> destroys one Skyhook by id, refusing a bad, unknown or structure-shaped one with text and answering a repeat gracefully; /ash unanchor here|<systemID> destroys every Skyhook in a system; both run the vendor destruction sequence per id, report every id they processed, and re-sync the game's item-id counter once when it is behind the highest id in use; /ash offset reads or sets how far past the landing point a Skyhook goes (kilometres or metres), saving the value so it survives a restart without touching the installer's config file; /ash anchor|unanchor region <regionID> works a whole region and system <systemID> one system, respecting NPC/faction space through the game's own sovereignty rule (a single NPC system is refused; inside a region those systems are skipped and named); a region run is paced and abortable - a countdown (cancelled by /ash stop with nothing done), then one system at a time, each verified against what was written and reported, with a configurable gap between systems, and /ash stop ends a run after the system being worked has been verified; /ash align moves the Skyhooks already deployed onto the configured offset, paced like a region run; multi-system runs warn the operator to stay in game, estimate their own duration from measured per-planet cost and report the actual time against it; /ash status reads the system back per planet as live, free, or free over a destroyed tombstone; /ash help lists the command set. Every subcommand also works as !ash in ordinary chat, so a character without staff rights can drive it. A planet that already has a live Skyhook, a structure-shaped Skyhook or a sovereignty ledger row for a real deployment is never built on twice; the free slot a claimed system gives an empty planet is where the Skyhook goes, and a destroyed Skyhook does not block a replacement - its tombstone is kept as history and the new one gets its own id. A conjured row matches a launched one in every field the game reads, including spaceRadius. Server-side only; no client change. Also installable with the third-party EveJS Launcher (settings panel, update channel and helper included).
